ModelA fails because Phi(median(|M|)/std) inherits the same conflation problem as Phi(mean/std) but in a different form: median(|M|) is sign-invariant but still couples magnitude with std which grows faster than typical magnitude. At n15 median/std SNR=1.017 gives Phi 0.845 vs 0.50 observed; at n20 SNR=0.690 gives 0.755 vs 0.565 observed.

ModelB fails because the training data is degenerate: proportion is exactly 0.0 at n=5 and n=10 (all margins negative due to small-n structure) and jumps to ~0.50 at n=15. A smooth a*n^b/(1+a*n^b) cannot fit this step with 4 points; best fit leaves 12.39pp error at n15 and R2=0.8797 below 0.90 threshold. This is a model-misspecification, not a sampling artifact.

Template invariance makes the diagnostic proportion(margin>0) near-exact but also makes model-based extrapolation questionable: under template invariance, sign fraction is deterministic given margins, but margins distribution itself may change at full DOM if template invariance breaks.

Extrapolation to n50=0.982 is gated behind failed C1/C2 and must not be used for product decisions. Its narrow PI90 [0.981,0.984] reflects bootstrap stability of the saturating fit, not epistemic validity of the extrapolation.

Small training set (4 points, n=5/10/15/20) with sign crossing between n10 and n15 limits power-law reliability. Fitting a*n^b/(1+a*n^b) with 2 parameters on 4 points leaves only 2 degrees of freedom; R2 threshold 0.90 is stringent for this step-like data.
